name: GenLimit.HallucinationModeCollapse.breadthIdentifier
type_kind: Bool/function-valued definition, not an identification theorem
reconstruction: For a family C, correct membership oracle O, arbitrary Bool-valued function Q of a finite list and a natural value, and input list xs, return the least candidate j at most length xs for which breadthMatches O Q xs j is true; if there is no such candidate, return 0. This is a named total finite-search function, not a theorem that it identifies C.
assumptions: C : Nat -> Set Nat is implicit and arbitrary.
O.query j x=true iff x belongs to C j, as required by MembershipOracle.
Q : List Nat -> Nat -> Bool is arbitrary. No support interpretation, correctness, computability or convergence premise for Q is present.
xs : List Nat is arbitrary; no consistency, presentation or witness condition is assumed.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: implicit C, then O, then Q, then xs, produce one Nat. With n=length(xs), choose firstTrue(breadthMatches O Q,xs,n+1) and apply Option.getD 0. Candidate range is j<n+1, equivalently j<=n; each match tests values x<n. There are no existential success witnesses in the declaration type.
defining_operation: Finite ascending candidate search; firstTrue preserves the earliest successful index. breadthMatches compares O.query j x against Q xs x OR listContains xs x for all natural x<n. The full list is passed to Q at every tested value; no persistent learner state appears. The code is given as finite recursion, not as a TruthTableProgram with a separately supplied fixed query batch.
effectiveness_boundary: Totality as a mathematical definition does not imply ordinary computability of O.query or Q. Conditional ordinary computability is a separate supplied theorem. No semantic identification or stabilization conclusion is included in this definition.
edge_cases: For xs=[], n=0, every breadthMatches result is vacuously true, and the only tested candidate is 0, so the output is 0.
If no candidate matches, output 0 can itself fail the match test; the output value does not distinguish failure from a genuine successful index 0.
The returned value is always at most n, but no full-language equality follows merely from a finite match.
A repeated observation can increase n and therefore expand both the numeric value-test window and candidate range, even without adding a distinct observed value.

name: GenLimit.HallucinationModeCollapse.breadthIdentifier_computable
reconstruction: For each implicit family C and correct membership oracle O, computability of the two-argument membership query implies that, for every Q whose two-argument function on finite lists and natural values is computable, the particular named function breadthIdentifier O Q is an ordinary computable map List Nat -> Nat.
assumptions: O : MembershipOracle C, including its exact semantic membership specification.
Q : List Nat -> Nat -> Bool, quantified after the membership-query computability premise.
Computable2 Q under the standard List Nat, Nat and Bool encodings. No correctness or support specification for Q is assumed.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: forall {C} O, Computable2(O.query) -> forall Q, Computable2(Q) -> Computable(breadthIdentifier O Q). This preserves the displayed binder/implication order. Canonical Nat encodings, the list encoding and Bool encoding are those explicitly shown in the exported type.
defining_operation: The conclusion is effectiveness of the same bounded first-match function above, using finite membership, boundedAll and firstTrue. It has no additional success check and no semantic target-language premise.
effectiveness_boundary: Both query-computability hypotheses are required by the signature. The result does not supply an effective Q, prove that an arbitrary support predicate is computable, or provide a mapping that extracts a single code uniformly from representations of all families. No runtime/rate bound or identification guarantee is stated.
edge_cases: No infinitude, family injectivity, least-index, tell-tale, subset-oracle or data-validity premise appears.
Q may be computable but have no relation to any generator or target; the theorem still concerns computation of the defined output, not correctness of that output.

name: GenLimit.HallucinationModeCollapse.breadthMatches
type_kind: Bool/function-valued definition, not an identification theorem
reconstruction: For any candidate j, returns true exactly when, for every natural number x strictly below length xs, membership in C j agrees with the disjunction of Q xs x and occurrence of x in the finite list xs. It compares a bounded initial segment of Boolean characteristic data; it does not compare entire languages.
assumptions: Implicit family C and correct membership oracle O.
Q : List Nat -> Nat -> Bool, input xs : List Nat and candidate j : Nat are arbitrary.
There is no hypothesis that Q is a support oracle, computes true fresh target membership, or satisfies a probability-law specification.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: implicit C, O, Q, xs, j -> Bool. Let n=length xs. Result=true iff forall x : Nat, x<n -> [O.query j x = (Q xs x OR (x occurs in xs))]. This Bool equality compares both true and false membership cases. There is no restriction on j in this definition.
defining_operation: boundedAll over x=0,...,n-1; each step compares a membership-query Bool to Q(xs,x).or(listContains xs x). listContains uses finite Nat equality. The observed-list membership term makes the right side true for any tested value already in xs, irrespective of Q at that value.
effectiveness_boundary: This definition uses oracle/function values without requiring them to be computable. It returns a Bool but has no separate effectiveness certificate in its type. The supplied breadthIdentifier_computable theorem assumes computability of both O.query and Q for the final learner.
edge_cases: At n=0 the bounded conjunction is true for every j and every Q.
Natural values x>=n are unconstrained, including observed values outside this numeric window. Consequently a match need not imply that all entries of xs lie in C j.
The OR does not require Q xs x to be false on observed values; Q may overlap the observed set.
List duplicates do not change the listContains bit, but can increase n; Q may also depend on order and duplicates because it receives the entire list.

name: GenLimit.HallucinationModeCollapse.eventually_leastMatching_of_target
reconstruction: For any family C and index z with no earlier index denoting the same set C z, there exists one natural cutoff T such that at every t>=T, every earlier i<z fails to agree with C z on all natural values below t. Equivalently, each earlier index has some membership disagreement below every sufficiently large t, with one cutoff simultaneous for all those indices.
assumptions: C : Nat -> Set Nat and z : Nat are implicit.
IsLeastTargetIndex C z means forall i<z, C i != C z. It is a condition on equality of denoted sets, not an inclusion-minimality condition.
No oracle, Q, learner, stream, observation list, computability or infinitude premise appears.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: forall {C} {z}, [forall i<z, C i != C z] -> exists T : Nat, forall t : Nat, T<=t -> forall i : Nat, i<z -> not [forall x : Nat, x<t -> (x in C i iff x in C z)]. T is chosen before t and i, so it is common to all smaller indices and all subsequent cutoffs; T may depend on C,z. The type gives no numeric bound or effective method for T.
defining_operation: A semantic finite-initial-segment separation statement. The parameter t bounds natural-number values, not sampled positions. No algorithm or update procedure is defined by this theorem; its proof body is absent.
effectiveness_boundary: No computability of family membership, no effective distinguishing value, no effective cutoff and no rate are supplied. In particular, this target has no breadthIdentifier or Q argument and states no equality or stabilization of learner outputs.
edge_cases: For z=0 there are no earlier indices; the conclusion is vacuous for that index range and a cutoff of 0 is compatible with it.
For t=0, MatchesInitialSegment is true for all i because there are no x<0; when smaller indices exist, the asserted eventual exclusion must occur at later cutoffs.
An earlier duplicate language would violate the premise. Duplicate languages at later indices are allowed.
Finite or empty target languages are permitted. The conclusion excludes earlier matches; it does not impose a uniform cutoff independent of C,z.
